newsitem.title: UK: "Shadow" UK MPC to hold inaugural meeting tonight.
newsitem.headline: "Shadow" UK MPC to hold inaugural meeting tonight.

text.p: A self-styled "shadow" UK Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) will hold its inaugural meeting this evening in a bid to contribute to the debate on the appropriate level of British interest rates.

"We felt that, particularly in view of the Bank of England's gaining independence, it was very important that there should be a debate," said Peter Spencer, chairman of the group and professor of financial economics at Birkbeck University.

Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown empowered the central bank's MPC to set interest rates in May. It has raised official British interest rates by 25 basis points in both June and July leaving them at 6.75 percent.

Members of the unofficial group have been selected for their expertise in monetary economics and include two former "wise men" -- members of the former government's panel of independent Treasury advisers: Cardiff University Professor Patrick Minford and Lombard Street Research economist Tim Congdon.

Most of the other members are also veterans on the UK economic scene: Alan Walters, economist at AIG Trading Group and erstwhile adviser to former British Premier Margaret Thatcher; Gordon Pepper, professor at City University business school; David Smith at Williams de Broe; Peter Warburton at Flemings.
The group also includes Cardiff University professor Kent Matthews, who will act as secretary; Anne Sibert, who is a senior lecturer at Birkbeck, and Greg Hess, who is a senior lecturer at Cambridge.
The group will be run under the auspices of the Institute for Economic affairs and the IEA's economics expert Colin Robinson will act as an observer.
"We've tried to get a mix of City people and academics. We've got a pretty wide-range of views," Spencer said.
The group intends to print minutes within a week of each quarterly meeting and to publish the results before the central bank's quarterly assessment of the economy.
The next meeting of the shadow MPC will be October 21.
